scopeReview: PSO-5.D.1: transport cost and market distance in rural land use, model assumptions and why specialty farming need not form concentric rings. Uses conditional perishability/bulk mechanisms, differing route rates, competing markets and environmental variation rather than requiring one universal modern crop order.
varietyReview: Four original stimuli: nested labeled market zones, two linear rent curves, equal-distance/different-rate route map and two-market price/distance table. Fifth check solves and substitutes the equal-bid threshold. Applications test refrigeration, historical fuelwood, model evidence and scale limitations; all four option explanations and varied keys.
repetitionReview: Four distinct assumption/representation tasks, not merely different crop names in the same calculation. Equal-bid threshold is separate from choosing at displayed distances. Model predictions are explicitly conditional, diagrams original and difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official framework and the model author’s academic transport-geography exposition checked for assumptions/logic; no diagram or lesson wording copied. All coordinates, rings, bids and prices original hypothetical examples. No new student resource or human-review claim.
